own_solution.law: Energy conservation: m_w c(T_i-T_f)=m_i L_f+m_i c T_f, with temperatures measured above the melting point. Thus T_f=23.4773 K and Q=m_w c(T_i-T_f)=34582.07 J.
assumptions: The supplied water heat capacity applies to both the original water and the melted ice throughout the temperature range.
The stated starting temperature applies before any added heater operation.
No heater supplies energy during equilibration.

defect_reasons.rendering_not_minimal: T2F5B and T162D specify only 'a small amount', whereas the other heater-temperature variants specify 17 K, violating the required preservation of the number and unit across variants.

notes: The base calorimetry problem is well-posed. The final description anchors the 40 K starting excess temperature before any heater operation, so heating the first container by 17 K makes its pre-contact excess temperature 57 K. Heating the isolated second container or describing an earlier run has no physical path to the requested heat transfer. The quantitative 17 K sentences agree in number and unit; the two 'small amount' sentences fail that variant requirement.
